#2691. Las Vegas expansion focus turns to new arena (which could be new Summer League home)

In the coming weeks (maybe), the NBA is expected to choose between three groups looking to own and run a new franchise in Las Vegas. While the biggest factor in the winning bid will always be the money — with bids expected to be at or above $10 billion — another topic has come to the forefront:

Specifically, one of the groups trying to win the bid — Golden Knights owner Bill Foley and former Suns owner Jerry Colangelo — has big plans for a new arena, which they detailed to Mike Vorkunov and Joe Vardon of The Athletic.

Foley's group reached out to USA Basketball and the NBA Summer League to discuss its interest in hosting them in a possible new arena if the group were to win the bid for a new Vegas franchise, according to multiple league sources briefed on the pitch.

There are two parts to that. As noted in the original report, USA Basketball is not moving its headquarters from Colorado Springs to Las Vegas. That said, the USA Men's National Team often starts its Olympics/World Cup training camps in Las Vegas, using UNLV's facilities and playing an exhibition game in the city. A new arena with top-flight facilities could be a draw for that kind of situation for USA teams.

The NBA Summer League is also held annually on the UNLV campus, with games played in the Thomas & Mack Arena and the Cox Pavilion, which are connected by a shared lobby (allowing Summer League to have two games going at once that fans can bounce between). Warren LeGarie, who runs the Summer League, told The Athletic he would be open to a new venue if it met the league's needs.

In the coming weeks, and certainly by the end of the year (per NBA Commissioner Adam Silver's previous comments), the league is expected to pick one of the three potential ownership groups in Las Vegas: Foley and Colangelo; Nancy Walton Laurie and her husband, Bill Laurie, with Lauri being a Walmart heir and Bill having owned the St. Louis Blues; former Bucks owner Marc Lasry, former Turner Broadcasting president David Levy and Canadian billionaire Steve Apostolopoulos.

All three potential ownership groups have talked about a new arena, potentially as an anchor for a resort/casino complex and entertainment district. Exactly where this new arena and resort would go is undecided, which is part of the delay. Dallas Mavericks governor Patrick Dumont — the CEO and chairman of Las Vegas Sands — led part of the discussion around the Las Vegas team at the Board of Governors' meeting before the season.

Getting a new arena designed, approved and built takes time and could mean the Las Vegas team will not tip off until the 2029-30 season.

While Las Vegas has the 10-year-old T-Mobile Arena just off the Strip — home to the NHL's Golden Knights, the WNBA's Aces, and where the NBA has hosted the final rounds of the midseason NBA Cup the past two years — it would need up to $400 million in renovations to host an NBA team, Silver has said. While not off the table, that is less likely than building a new arena.

Net ratings are courtesy of Cleaning the Glass and exclude garbage time.

#2686. Mike Macdonald says 'Sam's our quarterback' amid chatter that Drew Lock should start for Seahawks over Darnold

Drew Lock threw for 240 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions Sunday as the Seattle Seahawks secured a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

The Seahawks are now 4-0 this season with Lock, who's played objectively better than Sam Darnold in place of the injured Seattle starter in four appearances. This has prompted chatter amongst fans that maybe the Seahawks are better off with Lock as their full-time starting quarterback.

That chatter reached head coach Mike Macdonald on Monday. He was quick to shoot down the idea during an interview with Seattle Sports radio.

"Drew's been fantastic. He's been phenomenal," Macdonald said. "But Sam's our quarterback. … To have Drew as our backup and play the way he has has been awesome."

It's an interesting spot for the Seahawks. Darnold had the second-best season of his career in his first season with Seattle last year, and the Seahawks won a Super Bowl.

Seattle's defense and playmakers on offense in Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III were the primary driving forces of that championship run. But Darnold played his role well on a championship team. And moving away from a Super Bowl-winning quarterback the very next season could certainly be seen as a drastic step.

Drew Lock has been objectively better than Sam Darnold this season.

But outside of last season and his 2024 campaign with the Minnesota Vikings, Darnold's body of work leaves a lot to be desired. A former No. 3 draft pick, Darnold was firmly in bust territory after bouncing around and failing to hold jobs with the Jets, Panthers and 49ers before landing in Minnesota.

That version of Darnold is the one who's showed up in 2026.

In seven starts this season, including the season-opener in which he played just one possession due to injury, Darnold's completed 60.2% of his passes for 7 yards per attempt with 10 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. Those are generally not numbers fitting of an NFL starter. The Seahawks are 2-4 in Darnold's starts excluding the season-opener, and his turnovers are a significant reason why.

By comparison, Lock has completed 73.1% of his passes for 9 yards per attempt with 7 touchdowns and no interceptions. It's a small sample size from a career backup against a softer slate (Patriots, Cardinals, Cardinals, Raiders) than Darnold's faced (Commanders, Chargers, 49ers, Broncos, Chiefs, Bears). With two lost fumbles against the Raiders, Lock is not turnover free. But the numbers in his favor are compelling.

Macdonald, meanwhile, had to stop himself short with his praise of Darnold Monday before shifting to attribute Darnold's struggles to injury.

"We saw what Sam's been capable of both last year and in the — the beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said. … "Sam's our starting quarterback. I can't wait for him to be fully healthy probably for the first time."

The Seahawks have a bye this week. They'll come out of the bye for a key division showdown against the NFC-best 8-1 San Francisco 49ers on the other side.

Macdonald told reporters Monday that the Seahawks are "optimistic" that Darnold will be ready to return from a quadriceps injury to face the 49ers.

If he's healthy, expect Darnold to play. If he struggles in a Seahawks loss, expect this conversation to be renewed.

#2685. Joachim Löw impressed by Klopp's start as Germany boss but warns of setbacks

Joachim Löw has praised Jürgen Klopp for the start he has made as Germany head coach, having taken over from Julian Nagelsmann last summer following the disappointing World Cup round-of-32 exit against Paraguay.

“He is doing a very, very good job. He gives the players a lot of confidence and is trying to develop a sustainable playing philosophy. You get the feeling that things are heading in a positive direction,” Löw, who led Germany to World Cup glory in 2014, told Bild TV on Sunday.

Löw believes Klopp has already got plenty right, including his decision to name 44 players in his first squad and his handling of the controversy surrounding Felix Nmecha's religious crown celebration.

However, he also urged caution against raising expectations too high, with Germany having struggled to compete with the world's best since their World Cup triumph in 2014.

“His name alone does not always guarantee success. There will still be a few setbacks before we get back to that level,” Löw emphasised.

“The results are not all that important at this stage. We are in the Nations League now, and qualifying begins next year, which we will get through. The important thing will be for the team to spend six months playing together and building an understanding,” he said.

“You cannot expect any coach to get everything working within a few weeks. You have to look at whether there is progress,” Löw added.

Klopp and Germany will be hoping to secure a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals with a win over the Netherlands in their final Group A2 fixture on Monday.

COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Justin Pippen scored 12 of his 14 points in the second half, Jimmie Williams had 11 of his 13 before halftime, and Ohio State beat Prairie View A&M 86-59 on Monday.

It was the first meeting between the two programs. Ohio State improved to 12-0 against teams currently in the Southwestern Athletic Conference.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2682. Cleveland Browns proving that TD passes may be overrated

The Cleveland Browns continued to befuddle the NFL on Sunday with their latest comeback victory.

After falling behind 17-0 to the Houston Texans, the Browns did what they seem to do almost every week: the defense put a chokehold on the Texans, the offense slowly found its footing, and when Quinshon Judkins crossed the goal line with 53 seconds remaining, the Browns had their sixth victory of the season.

No one can really explain how the Browns are doing it, not even the coaches or the players themselves, but they're doing it because Cleveland has followed the same basic script in each of their six victories.

Chief among the reasons that the Browns find themselves in a hole each week, but also one of the key reasons they have been able to overcome those deficits, has been the play of quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has generally been poor to bad for the first three quarters of each game, only to come alive in the fourth quarter.

Watson has been especially effective in the final two minutes of games, as Pro Football Focus highlighted after Sunday's win, as Watson is:

That last bullet point is an interesting one, given a narrative that has emerged surrounding Watson, as his detractors are eager to point out that he has not thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5 against the New York Jets.

But you know who did throw touchdown passes on Sunday?

Cam Ward had two for the Tennessee Titans and lost

Tyler Shough had one for the New Orleans Saints and lost

Dak Prescott had five for the Dallas Cowboys and lost

Aaron Rodgers had two for the Pittsburgh Steelers, and oh boy did they lose.

Touchdown passes are fun and can make for great highlights, and there is no doubt Watson would love to have back that errant pass to Jerry Jeudy on Sunday that would have been a walk-in touchdown. But they are just one part of the bigger goal: outscore your opponent by any means necessary.

Think back to the three touchdowns the Browns scored on Sunday:

Watson had a six-yard run after hitting Jeudy on a 65-yard pass

KC Concepcion had a six-yard run to finish a drive that included an 18-yard pass to Malachi Corley

Judkins scored the game-winner on a five-yard run to finish a drive that featured a 30-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr.

Would it have made any difference if any of those scores had come on a pass instead of a run? Unless the NFL changes its rules overnight, a touchdown still counts as six points no matter how it is scored.

Think back to all those times over the years when the Browns have been in a first-and-goal situation only to bumble their way into a turnover or settle for a field goal instead of a touchdown. The type of drive that goes something like a run on first down for minus-2 yards, a sack on second down, then an incompletion on third down that deflates a once-promising drive.

At some point, Watson will throw another touchdown and another nonsensical narrative will die from a lack of oxygen.

As long as the Browns finish more of their drives with touchdowns than field goals, does it really matter if they do it via the run or the pass?

#2680. French cricket 'dying' as federation crisis and chaos deepens

Cricket in France is at risk of disappearing altogether, less than two years before the sport makes its long-awaited Olympic return.

The last, and only time that cricket was played at the Olympics was in Paris in 1900, where England beat France by 158 runs to win the gold medal.

France will not be at the Twenty20 tournament at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, and cricket in the country is on the verge of "dying" due to a crisis within the country's federation, Miriam Romero, a player and administrator, told AFP.

Clubs suspended the national league this year as they try to force president Prebagarane 'Prebou' Balane to resign following a series of scandals.

The organisation lost its recognition by France's sports ministry early this year, while the International Cricket Council (ICC) in June suspended development funding and placed France Cricket on notice for "non-compliance with membership criteria".

This came after scandals such as 'ghost' women's matches and development funding that was unaccounted for.

"We must not let cricket die in France, it's a shame," Romero, who is president of the Paris regional cricket committee, told AFP.

Romero, who at 65 still plays, was previously on France Cricket's finance committee and is also a director at Paris Universitaire Club (PUC), one of the main cricket clubs in France.

She says PUC and other clubs have left France Cricket and are trying to set up a new national association to replace the existing structure.

Others, though, simply want Balane to resign so they can resolve the governance issues that saw them lose recognition from the ICC and the sports ministry.

According to the minutes of a board meeting in June, seen by the France 24 television station before it was deleted from the France Cricket website, Balane said he would resign on July 17.

But board member Jubaid Ahamed said Balane had not fulfilled his promise.

Despite repeated attempts by AFP to contact Balane and France Cricket, neither replied.

The chaos led the main clubs in France Cricket's domestic championship to suspend the competition in mid-August, meaning the season was never completed.

They have had enough and their demands are simple: "Firstly, to change the president. Then, to restructure France Cricket by implementing more flexible rules to develop youth and women's cricket," Djega Sankaran, the former president of the Morangis club, south of Paris, said.

He said he had resigned so he could speak freely without repercussions for his club.

AFP spoke to the president of the France Gymkhana club, Rizwan Babri, the president of another club and the team manager from a third club who all confirmed they wanted Balane to resign and for France Cricket to be restructured.

One person described Balane as acting like "God Almighty", another accused him of treating the federation as "his private affair".

In November, 34 clubs -- more than enough to reach the necessary one third threshold -- asked France Cricket for an extraordinary general meeting to submit a motion of no confidence in Balane and the executive committee, but the president refused, in email responses seen by AFP.

The crisis had been brewing for some time.

It began when France 24 broke an explosive story in 2023 about clubs in the country faking women's matches, apparently so France Cricket could benefit from hundreds of thousands of dollars of ICC funding.

The national women's cricket team wrote an open letter demanding an investigation and accountability, but instead, France Cricket suspended them.

"What was sad for us was that the men, the other clubs, did not support us," Sabine Lieury, a former French women's international and ex-president of Nantes Cricket Club, told AFP.

"The cricket world didn't want to rebel with the French girls to say that this was unacceptable."

Worst of all, the men's national team accused the women of being "cry-babies" and disloyal.

"No one did anything, they kept playing to protect themselves."

But they changed their tune after France Cricket lost its ICC development funding and French government recognition.

France Cricket have always denied that women's ghost matches took place -- Balane told the BBC in June that it had "never" happened.

But that was not true. In fact, it was still happening last year.

The problem was that the federation obliged clubs to set up a women's team and threatened them with fines or even demotion if they did not fulfil fixtures.

Some clubs tried, but there was not the necessary interest to do so in such a tight timeframe.

"Everyone brought women's teams one way or another, with cousins, but it was just to avoid Prebou's sanctions," said Sankaran, who was heavily involved in trying to develop cricket in the Ile de France region around Paris.

"There were six people here, four people there. There were no (real) matches."

In the end, it was easier not to have a women's team.

"There were agreements between clubs: 'You won't get a fine and I won't get a fine'. They made up the scores," said Sankaran. "All the clubs made mistakes, me included."

But those who were playing had always been suspicious.

There were four teams in the French women's first division at that time: Nantes, PUC, Lille and Lisses. But there were nine teams in the second division, and none were ever promoted.

"How is it that every year, we never see someone coming from these second division teams?" said Lieury.

"When the scandal broke, we were shocked, but at the same time, we said: 'we're not surprised, we've never seen these girls'."

Even in 2024 and 2025, only two clubs -- PUC and AC Stains -- could muster a full women's team and genuinely fulfil fixtures.

Tara Britton, a former Lisses and France player who subsequently joined PUC, said the only genuine match her new team played was against Stains.

The other teams either did not turn up, did so without enough players, or wanted to play with a tennis ball rather than a cricket ball.

The France Cricket website lists the results from 2024 and 2025 with PUC as the champions and Stains as the beaten "finalists".

But Britton said those seasons essentially amounted to a single match.

And then there is the question of the ICC development funding.

Numerous clubs told AFP that they never received any help from France Cricket. Sankaran said the organisation even refused to contribute to the purchase of a plastic wicket or cricket nets, offering only a loan instead.

#2678. NFL news, live updates: Aidan Hutchinson reportedly suffers torn ACL on sack celebration; Patriots QB Drake Maye out indefinitely with ankle injury

Another NFL Sunday is in the books, with just one game left in Week 10 as the Baltimore Ravens host the LA Chargers on "Monday Night Football."

Sunday kicked off with a bang as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots faced off in Munich, Germany, with injuries to two stars that will have all eyes drawn as the new week plays out. Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered what is feared to be a season-ending ACL tear while celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye … who suffered an ankle injury on that very sack, which knocked him out of the game and could cost him the season.

Week 10 also offered us our first look at Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a starter. He led scoring drives on each of the Raiders' first two possessions and entered halftime with a 10-7 lead over the Seattle Seahawks, but Drew Lock rallied with two passing touchdowns in the third quarter to take the lead, improving to 3-0 as a starter for Seattle this season. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers exited the loss with an ankle injury.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 10.

Dallas Cowboys right guard Tyler Booker sustained a high ankle sprain during the second quarter of Sunday's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and is expected to miss at least four weeks, according to several reports.

Such an injury usually requires a recovery timeline of four to six weeks, but the Cowboys are hopeful that Booker can return in three to four weeks.

Starting cornerback DaRon Bland also suffered a right high ankle sprain during the Cowboys' first defensive series while trying to tackle 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. He had dealt with an injury to his left ankle during the previous week of practice.

The team is also considering whether or not to put both plalyers on injured reserve with a possible four-week absence. However, Dallas has a bye for Week 14, which could allow them to stay on the active roster.

The Chicago Bears should have running back Kyle Monangai available for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

Monangai has been out for more than a month with both a thumb injury and turf toe.

"It's something I can manage now," he said, via ESPN's Courtney Cronin. "The time off was needed though for sure. I feel in a much better spot than I was a month ago."

The two big Super Bowl odds movers this week resulted from one play on Sunday, when Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye and then Hutchinson proceeded to injure himself on the celebration.

Unfortunately, for the Lions, it's reportedly a torn ACL for Hutchinson, which would sideline him for the rest of the season. Detroit, despite a 7-2 record, moved from 18-1 to 20-1 odds to win the Super Bowl (11th-best odds). It's also reportedly a "significant lower-leg injury" for Maye, and with a 5-5 record already in a crowded AFC field, New England's Super Bowl odds tumbled from 28-1 entering the week to 66-1.

Here are the current Super Bowl odds for every NFL team at BetMGM sportsbooks:

Chicago Bears, Jacksonville Jaguars: +750

Cincinnati Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs: 10-1

Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks: 16-1

New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers: 66-1

Dallas Cowboys, Houston Texans, New York Giants, Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 80-1

Cleveland Browns, Washington Commanders: 150-1

Las Vegas Raiders, New Orleans Saints: 500-1

Arizona Cardinals, Indianapolis Colts, Los Angeles Chargers, Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Philadelphia Eagles, Tennessee Titans: 2,000-1

The Chargers are bringing in some reinforcements ahead of a Monday night clash against the Ravens. The team announced Monday that they have activated tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman from injured reserve.

Njoku has been marked out with a fibula injury, while Perryman has been out with a pectoral injury. Both players were listed as "questionable" heading into this weekend, but were full participants in practice on Saturday.

In related moves, Los Angeles placed guard/tackle Branson Taylor on IR and elevated defensive lineman Myles Adams from the practice squad.

The 0-8 Chargers are trying to pick up their first win of the year against Baltimore.

The Raiders have some good news on star tight end Brock Bowers, who exited Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with an ankle injury. Though the injury, which occurred during the first quarter, initially appeared concerning, Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that things were better than originally feared.

In a press conference, Kubiak said that the team was "still evaluating" Bowers, but that the tight end will be day-to-day with the injury.

"It's not as bad as we thought, but still is a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said.

Bowers, who missed the first two games of the season after undergoing minor knee surgery, leads Las Vegas in receiving with 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games.

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

The change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling in the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

The Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

If everything goes according to plan, star Green Bay defensive end Micah Parsons should be returning from injury sooner rather than later.

In a press conference on Monday, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that the "plan" is for Parsons to play in Green Bay's next game, with the team taking on the Los Angeles Rams the day before Thanksgiving.

"Well, that's my plan, but I think my plan's been different than everybody else's the whole time," LaFleur said with a smile, after being asked if the plan was for Parsons to return to the field in L.A. "There's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before we can definitively say that he's a go. He's showing progress, but we'll see where he is by the end of the week."

Parsons was cleared for practice earlier this month, 11 months after tearing his ACL.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison has a thumb injury that requires surgery and will miss multiple weeks.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed the injury on Monday, telling reporters that Addison sustained a "freak" injury in practice last week. O'Connell did not reveal the precise nature of Addison's injury or how he sustained it.

Addison missed Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers and may need a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games.

Seattle Seahawks running back George Holani suffered a sprained MCL in Week 10's 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports.

Seattle has a bye next week, so the hope is that will provide enough recovery time to avoid putting Holani on injured reserve, according to Rapoport.

Holani did not have a carry in Sunday's contest after leaving in the first quarter. In 10 games this season, he has 117 yards on 37 carries with 1 touchdown. Additionally, Holani has registered 12 receptions for 88 yards.

With starting QB Baker Mayfield dealing with a lower-body injury through the team's bye week, Tampa Bay opted to sign veteran Cooper Rush to the roster, his agents announced.

Rush began the season with the Falcons. In two games, he threw for 229 yards with a touchdown and four interceptions. He was released once Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa were healthy enough to return.

Tampa Bay has the Detroit Lions, Carolina Panthers, Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens over the next month.

The Dolphins have waived veteran kicker Zane Gonzalez. He played four games for Miami this year.

Gonzalez ends his Dolphins tenure 6 of 10 on field goals and 6 of 7 on extra-point attempts.

The Miami kicker missed two field goals (47 yards, 51 yards) and an extra point in the Dolphins' 24 to 22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

Miami currently has no other kicker in the organization.

Detroit Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson reportedly tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye, per NFL Network.

Early reports Sunday suggested Hutchinson was dealing with a "significant" knee injury. Initial tests reportedly confirmed as much Monday.

Hutchinson will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season as he recovers from the injury. It's unclear whether his availability will be impacted next season.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are currently on bye, but unfortunately, they are still in the news.

Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is dealing with a lower-leg injury that he suffered during last week's loss to the Chicago Bears, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported on Sunday morning.

Mayfield's status is uncertain for Tampa Bay's Week 11 matchup with the Detroit Lions. It is unclear where Mayfield picked up the injury against the Bears. The quarterback was sacked four times, but he never left the game. This week, he was reportedly spotted in a walking boot, rehabbing and resting.

This would not be the first time this season the Buccaneers have played without their starting quarterback. Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3, which kept him out for three games. Tampa Bay turned to undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who went 1-2 as the starter.

Mayfield has played in six games so far this season and is 2-4. He has not looked like himself all year, throwing for just 922 yards, 3 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. In a bad-weather Week 8 game against the Atlanta Falcons, he finished 0-for-3 for zero yards in the team's 16-0 win, making infamous history.

A frustrating season for Los Angeles Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey will continue in Week 10. While the receiver was initially listed as questionable on the team's final injury report, he will not play against the Baltimore Ravens on "Monday Night Football."

McConkey was ruled out for the game due to back spasms. He did not travel with the team to Baltimore, the Chargers announced.

McConkey has been limited by multiple injuries throughout the regular season. He was held to just 35 yards in Week 2 thanks to a rib injury and missed Week 5 due to a foot issue.

He caught just one ball in Week 6 before resting during the bye week. While the wideout looked to be close to 100 percent with an 86-yard performance in Week 8, McConkey missed Week 9 with back spasms. The injury reportedly occurred just before game time. He was expected to play in the contest.

Those back spasms have apparently continued to plague McConkey throughout the week. He was held out of practice each day leading up to Week 10, though the team still held some hope he would play, initially giving him the questionable tag.

But the issue was bad enough that the team opted against throwing McConkey on the field Monday night.

Raiders tight end Brock Bowers reportedly avoided a major ankle injury in Week 10. Bowers will have more tests done Monday, but the early indication is that he's more day-to-day.

Bowers left Sunday's game against the Seahawks due to the issue. He finished with just 18 yards.

The injury put a damper on the debut of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who lost his best receiver in the contest.

The New England Patriots could be without quarterback Drake Maye for the rest of the season. Maye may have sustained a serious leg injury during Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions, with the Patriots fearing a possible ankle fracture.

Maye did not travel to the United States with the team after Sunday's game, staying in Germany to undergo additional tests. Those tests could reveal whether Maye needs surgery.

No matter what those tests reveal, Maye is looking at an extended absence, if not a season-ending one.

Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson made his presence known early against the New England Patriots. On the Patriots' first offensive drive, Hutchinson broke through the line on third down and sacked Drake Maye.

Following the play, Hutchinson got up to celebrate the sack. He jumped into the air and immediately fell to the ground after landing. Hutchinson appeared to be holding his right knee.

Hutchinson walked off the field, but headed straight to the medical tent on the sideline. He was later spotted on the broadcast heading to the locker room.

He was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury, but late in the third quarter, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Detroit eventually cruised to a 35-10 victory.

Early reports suggested Hutchinson may have sustained a "significant" knee injury, per NFL Network. Detroit is reportedly not expecting good news. While a second opinion is coming, it's possible Hutchinson will not return this season.

#2676. Jordan Walsh continues to play himself into Boston’s lineup

Going into Sunday's game against the Dallas Mavericks, I saw what Joe Mazzulla had in store for the Boston Celtics starting lineup. It was nothing out of the ordinary, but I found myself questioning why Jordan Walsh was still a part of it.

This was Walsh's eight start of the season out of 13 games, tied with Neemias Queta for the fourth most starts this season. The two of them trail only Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Derrick White, the obvious core of the team.

Clearly, Mazzulla sees something in Jordan. Why else would he continue to trust him night in, and night out?

In Sunday's rout of the Mavericks, a 131-94 victory for the Celtics, Walsh showed exactly how he earned the trust of his coach. He's not going to be a big box score guy on a nightly basis, but he will still make his presence felt through grit, hard-nosed defense, and a whole lot of hustle.

Boston took a historic lead against Dallas in the first quarter, ending the period up 42 to 9, the second-largest first quarter scoring differential in NBA history. Jordan had his fingerprints all over the game as the Celtics built their lead.

From the jump, Boston's defense was hounding the Mavericks, with Jordan Walsh being at the center of several possessions. Though the Celtics defense relies on plenty of switching, Jordan mostly found himself picking up Cooper Flagg and Naji Marshall, the two primary ball-handlers for Dallas.

Walsh's matchups weren't bold enough to take a single field goal attempt in the quarter while he was the primary defender. Not only that, but Jordan was able to force two turnovers. He picked off a Marshall pass for Flagg which he took back for a tough transition bucket with a foul on one possession, and drew an illegal screen from Daniel Gafford not long after.

In addition to his on-ball defense, Walsh was incredibly active off the ball, stunting drives and showing his hands to disrupt the Mavericks possessions while giving his teammates an extra second to get back in step with their matchups.

When Jordan ultimately went to the bench for the first time, Boston held a 22-4 lead. All four of Dallas's points came at the freethrow line. Meanwhile, Walsh was responsible for eight of Boston's 22 points, tying his career-high for most points in the first quarter.

All of that being said, Jordan is far from a finished product. What he does have is an unbreakable spirit, and a desire to improve. He's still a few months away from turning 23 years old, so even though it feels like he's been around for a while, there's plenty of untapped potential in there which we can see shine through on nights like this.

Walsh made a rare podium appearance after the game, and provided us with some insight into how he views his role at this point. He explained how his value isn't defined by the box score, saying "it's never really about shots and points. It's about 'what can I create for the team?' Can I create a situation where they can't help off me? Can I create a situation where Cooper Flagg isn't bringing the ball up the court and it's somebody else? That's how I find my way into the game."

When asked about his confidence as a defender he said "I think I'm the best defender. Every game is guarding the best player, and obviously the team, the organization believes I can do that every night so that's why they put me on that guy. That in and of itself gives me the confidence to go out there and try to do the best I can."

Mazzulla gave some encouraging words to compliment that sentiment as well, saying "I think Jodan's continuing to develop the mindset that we need him to have versus great players. And a great team has to have a group of guys that they can rely on to make it difficult for the team's best player every single day… Jordan's on that list."

Walsh even got a shoutout from Tatum in the press room, who added that Jordan, along with Baylor Scheierman, Hugo Gonzalez, and Ron Harper Jr., is more than capable in the starting spot. "Whether it's on the defensive end, or knocking down shots, or crashing, those guys have been really, really good."

Clearly, the team is behind Walsh, and believes in his ability to contribute to the team. Don't be surprised while we continue to see him in the starting lineup, or even when he has a big night off the bench.

#2675. College Football Playoff Scenarios Entering Week 12: Who Is Safe and Who Still Needs Help?

Two weeks remain in the college football regular season, and the College Football Playoff race finally looks manageable.

PFN's Playoff Meter now projects only a small group of teams with realistic paths to the 12-team field. Georgia, Alabama, Utah, Notre Dame, Boise State, Miami, Texas, UCLA, Indiana, Tennessee, Wake Forest, BYU, and Texas Tech all have at least a 50% chance to make the playoff. Oregon and Iowa are the only other teams above 10%.

That is a much tighter race than we had even one week ago.

Cam Miller and Max Chadwick worked through each conference entering Week 12, identifying the teams that can essentially play their way in and the few remaining contenders that still need outside help.

Note: The selection committee's latest published rankings are from Nov. 10. Its next rankings will be released Nov. 17. PFN's Playoff Meter probabilities below incorporate results through Nov. 15.

The SEC is trending toward four playoff teams.

PFN gives Georgia a 100% chance to make the field, Alabama 99.8%, Texas 95.7%, and Tennessee 84.5%.

Kentucky's loss to Florida effectively ended its realistic at-large hopes, while LSU's fourth loss took the Tigers out of the conversation. That leaves four teams separated from everyone else in the conference.

Georgia is 9-1 after beating Missouri 48-21 and has a 99.6% chance to reach the SEC Championship Game.

The Bulldogs close the regular season at South Carolina before hosting Georgia Tech.

Chadwick sees virtually no path for Georgia to miss the playoff.

"They're the best team in college football right now," Chadwick said.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

PFN's numbers agree. Georgia has a 100% playoff probability and a 28.2% chance to win the national championship, the highest mark in the Playoff Meter.

Even one late loss should do little more than change Georgia's seed. The Bulldogs have beaten Alabama and have spent the past month handling ranked opponents comfortably.

Alabama is 8-2 after beating Vanderbilt 21-6 and has essentially secured an at-large safety net.

The Crimson Tide have only a 31.9% chance to reach the SEC Championship Game, but PFN gives them a 99.8% chance to make the playoff.

Alabama hosts Chattanooga in Week 12 before closing with the Iron Bowl. Even a loss to Auburn would leave the Crimson Tide with the type of résumé the committee has already rewarded.

The committee ranked Alabama No. 3 before its latest victory, and Chadwick believes the Crimson Tide could probably survive another loss if necessary.

Texas survived LSU 22-21 to improve to 8-2.

The Longhorns haven't made things easy on themselves, but their collection of ranked wins has created a strong at-large case. PFN now gives Texas a 95.7% playoff probability.

Arkansas visits Austin in Week 12 before Texas closes against Texas A&M.

Chadwick believes Texas could potentially survive another loss because of the strength at the top of its résumé, but the easiest path doesn't require testing that theory.

Tennessee's playoff probability climbed to 84.5% after a 22-7 win at Texas A&M.

The Volunteers now host LSU before closing against Vanderbilt.

A loss to LSU wouldn't automatically end Tennessee's season, but it would create far more uncertainty than exists for Georgia, Alabama, or Texas. Chadwick views Week 12 as Tennessee's most important remaining test.

If the Volunteers win, they should enter the final week in excellent at-large position.

The Big 12 suddenly has a realistic path to three playoff bids.

Utah is nearly certain to make the field at 99.7%. BYU sits at 64.3%, while Texas Tech has climbed to 58.4% after scoring 52 points in a win at Oklahoma State.

PFN's simulations currently project 2.23 Big 12 bids on average.

Utah improved to 10-0 by surviving Arizona 40-39 and has a 99.7% chance both to make the playoff and reach the Big 12 Championship Game.

The Utes finish at TCU and against West Virginia.

DIVE IN: PFN's Free CFB HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More

Chadwick believes Utah only needs to win one of those two games to remove any realistic playoff doubt, regardless of what happens in the conference title game.

The larger question is whether Utah can stay unbeaten and earn a top-four seed.

The Cougars have only a 34% chance to reach the Big 12 Championship Game, but a 64.3% chance to make the playoff.

That means their most likely route is as an at-large team.

BYU plays at Kansas in Week 12 before closing with Cincinnati. Chadwick's view is simple: The Cougars probably have to win both.

At 10-2, BYU could sit at home during championship weekend while other bubble teams risk taking another loss.

That creates the possibility of an ironic reversal from 2025, when BYU went to the Big 12 title game, lost, and was left out.

Texas Tech's playoff odds jumped from 28.9% to 58.4% after Week 11.

The Red Raiders are 9-1 and have found another level offensively with Thomas Castellanos at quarterback.

They close at Baylor and against TCU and now have a 65.2% chance to reach the Big 12 Championship Game.

Chadwick believes Texas Tech is becoming one of the more dangerous teams in the field, but a conference title game loss could create the selection committee's most difficult argument.

An 11-2 Texas Tech team could be compared directly with an 11-2 Wake Forest or a 10-2 BYU team for one of the final spots.

That is one of the few playoff debates that may not be resolved until championship weekend.

The Big Ten race has narrowed to UCLA and Indiana as the clear playoff favorites.

UCLA has a 93.9% chance to make the field. Indiana sits at 88.4%.

Oregon and Iowa are both down at 14.2%, while Ohio State has fallen to 4.8%.

UCLA remains undefeated after beating Illinois 22-14.

The Bruins now travel to Michigan before finishing against USC.

Their 92.6% chance to reach the Big Ten Championship Game reflects how much margin Bob Chesney's team has created. A win over either Michigan or USC may be enough to keep UCLA in excellent at-large position even if it later loses the conference title game.

The defense remains the foundation. UCLA has consistently won the type of games the program struggled to finish in previous seasons.

Indiana beat USC 27-13 and now has an 88.4% playoff probability.

The Hoosiers play at Washington before closing with Purdue.

Chadwick believes Indiana only needs to handle its remaining schedule to secure a bid. Even one win may be enough to keep the Hoosiers in strong position, while winning both would remove the debate entirely.

A UCLA-Indiana Big Ten Championship Game would match Bob Chesney against Curt Cignetti, two coaches whose recent paths ran through James Madison.

Oregon is 7-3 and still has a 19% chance to reach the Big Ten Championship Game. Iowa is 8-2 but has only a 3.4% chance to play for the conference title.

Both teams sit at 14.2% to make the playoff.

Iowa's problem is résumé strength. Its best wins haven't aged well enough to make a 10-2 record an automatic at-large case.

Oregon has the stronger high-end profile but already carries three losses.

Ohio State is even farther back. The Buckeyes have only a 4.8% playoff probability and likely need to find their way into, and then win, the Big Ten Championship Game.

For all three, simply winning out may not be enough.

Miami and Wake Forest are separating from the rest of the ACC.

Miami has a 98.6% playoff probability and is already at 100% to reach the ACC Championship Game in PFN's simulations. Wake Forest is at 82.5% to make the playoff and 98.4% to reach Charlotte.

Louisville is the next ACC team at only 0.5%.

Miami rebounded from its Notre Dame loss by beating Duke 36-25.

The Hurricanes close with Virginia Tech and Boston College, two games PFN heavily favors them to win.

If Miami reaches 11-1, Chadwick sees little chance the Hurricanes miss the playoff regardless of the ACC Championship Game result.

A regular-season upset would change the calculus. A 10-3 Miami team with a championship-game loss would create a much more difficult at-large case.

Wake Forest's 49-7 demolition of SMU was one of Week 11's biggest statements.

The Demon Deacons are now 9-1, and their playoff probability jumped 28.4 percentage points to 82.5%.

They close against Georgia Tech and Duke.

Chadwick and Miller both view Wake Forest as one of the 12 best teams in the country right now. The concern isn't quality. It's what happens if the Demon Deacons reach the ACC Championship Game and lose to Miami for a second time.

That could leave an 11-2 Wake Forest competing with BYU and Texas Tech for the final at-large spots.

The cleanest solution is obvious: Keep winning and then beat Miami in Charlotte.

Notre Dame's 99.6% playoff probability makes the Fighting Irish one of the safest teams in the country.

The Irish are 9-1 after beating Boston College 41-7 and host SMU before finishing at Syracuse.

Notre Dame's win over Miami gives it the résumé anchor it needs. Chadwick believes the Irish could probably survive one late loss and still remain in the field.

At 11-1, the larger question becomes whether Notre Dame can climb high enough for a first-round bye.

New Mexico's loss and the narrowing American Conference race changed everything for Boise State.

PFN gives the Broncos a 99.6% chance to make the playoff, up from 68.9% one week earlier.

Boise State is 9-1 and closes against San Diego State and Utah State before the Pac-12 Championship Game.

DIVE IN: PFN's NFL Draft HQ: Draft Prospect Analysis, Stats & Info

The 2026 playoff format guarantees one bid to the highest-ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12, or Sun Belt. That team does not have to be a conference champion.

That distinction gives Boise State significant protection.

The Broncos already own wins over Memphis and Western Michigan, two of the stronger contenders from other Group of Six conferences. Their only loss came at Oregon.

Chadwick believes Boise State can probably afford one loss over its final three games and still own the strongest résumé in the Group of Six.

The playoff field isn't set, but most of the available seats have clear favorites.

Georgia, Alabama, Utah, Notre Dame, Boise State, Miami, Texas, UCLA, Indiana, and Tennessee all enter Week 12 above an 84% playoff probability.

That leaves the most interesting fight among Wake Forest, BYU, and Texas Tech.

All three can remove most of the ambiguity by winning. The complication comes if Texas Tech or Wake Forest reaches a conference championship game and loses while BYU sits at home.

That is the scenario where the committee will have to decide how much it values a championship-game appearance against an at-large team that avoided the extra loss.

Two weeks remain before those arguments become real.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

#2673. Browns schedule: Bye week is followed by some interesting matchups

Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season concludes on Monday Night Football, but Cleveland Browns fans get two weeks to relax and enjoy their team's 6-4 start to the season and holding a current spot in the AFC Playoff picture. The bye week comes at a perfect time, according to HC Todd Monken, as the coaching staff will get a better chance to self-scout for the closing schedule.

Perhaps that will help Cleveland start faster after the same concern has popped up week after week, including in their Week 10 victory over the Houston Texans.

Either way, the time off will be good for the players' bodies, while the coaches rework the plan. As of now, the Browns do not play again until November 29th at 1 PM against the Las Vegas Raiders. "As of now" is important, as the NFL can flex that game to Sunday Night Football instead of the early slot. That decision will have to be made by Tuesday.

After facing the Raiders, with rookie QB Fernando Mendoza, Cleveland then welcomes the Cincinnati Bengals, the current AFC North leaders, and the Atlanta Falcons, led by their former head coach Kevin Stefanski, to finish off their four-game homestand.

That leaves a finishing stretch with three out of four on the road: at the New York Giants, at the Baltimore Ravens, at home with the Indianapolis Colts, and finishing on the road against the Bengals again.

Seven games, four at home and three on the road, starting with six wins on the record books coming out of the bye week. Some juicy storylines are included in that schedule as well. If the Browns can win two of the next three, Cleveland fans will start the 12 Days of Christmas with a clear sight of the NFL playoffs, and that is all we can ask for.

#2670. College Football Power Rankings Week 12: Georgia, Utah, UCLA Lead Max Chadwick’s Top 12

Week 11 made the top of college football easier to separate from the rest of the country.

Georgia and Utah remain the two teams Max Chadwick is most comfortable putting at the top. UCLA is still undefeated, Notre Dame has one of the best wins in the country, and Miami rebounded after its first loss.

The selection committee ranked the Crimson Tide No. 3 before Week 11, but Chadwick doesn't believe their résumé belongs that high even after another convincing win.

Here is Chadwick's personal top 12 entering Week 12.

Note: The attached recording verbalizes Chadwick's ranking through No. 12. It does not state the order from Nos. 13-25, so those teams are not reconstructed here from the unseen on-screen graphic.

The Bulldogs improved to 9-1 by beating Missouri 48-21, continuing a stretch in which their only real blemish is the loss to Auburn.

Chadwick acknowledged that Utah has a reasonable argument for the top spot because the Utes remain undefeated.

He still prefers Georgia because of how dominant the Bulldogs have looked against quality competition.

Georgia's win over Alabama remains one of the strongest results on any résumé. Since the Auburn loss, the Bulldogs have also handled Florida, Ole Miss, and Missouri without creating much late-game doubt.

PFN's Playoff Meter gives Georgia a 28.2% chance to win the national championship, comfortably the best probability in the country.

Utah is the obvious alternative at No. 1.

The Utes are 10-0 after surviving Arizona 40-39, with Devin Dampier accounting for four touchdowns and throwing the game-winning 70-yard score to Creed Whittemore late in the fourth quarter.

The résumé includes BYU and Arizona, and Utah is the only undefeated Big 12 team left.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Chadwick still gives Georgia the edge because of its week-to-week dominance, but Utah has done the one thing Georgia hasn't: avoid losing.

The Utes travel to TCU in Week 12 with a 99.7% chance to make the playoff.

This is where Chadwick makes his first major departure from the committee.

UCLA was No. 4 in the Nov. 10 CFP rankings, one spot behind Alabama. Chadwick would move the Bruins ahead of the Crimson Tide.

UCLA is 10-0 after beating Illinois 22-14 and has consistently leaned on one of the best defenses in college football.

Chadwick and Miller highlighted defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler's work and a unit led by players such as linebacker Tamiya Osemigo.

The schedule hasn't been as strong as Alabama's, but an undefeated Big Ten team this late in November has done enough for Chadwick to put it third.

Notre Dame has continued moving upward since beating Miami.

The Fighting Irish are 9-1 after a 41-7 win over Boston College, and Chadwick believes the head-to-head victory over the Hurricanes gives Notre Dame one of the strongest arguments among the one-loss teams.

That combination is enough for Chadwick to move Notre Dame ahead of Alabama as well.

PFN's Playoff Meter gives the Irish a 99.6% chance to make the field and a 16.8% chance to win the national championship, second only to Georgia.

Miami drops behind Notre Dame because of the head-to-head result but remains in Chadwick's top five.

The Hurricanes beat Duke 36-25 to move to 9-1 and remain undefeated in ACC play.

Darian Mensah continues to give Miami one of the nation's most efficient passing attacks even without injured receiver Malachi Toney.

The loss at Notre Dame is significant, but it isn't enough to erase everything Miami did before it.

With Virginia Tech and Boston College remaining, the Hurricanes are in excellent position to reach the ACC Championship Game at 11-1.

Texas remains one of the hardest teams in the country to evaluate.

The Longhorns have two losses to teams that were unranked at the time, Oklahoma and Florida.

Texas escaped LSU 22-21 and has accumulated one of the strongest collections of high-end victories in the country.

DIVE IN: PFN's Free CFB HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More

Chadwick puts more weight on those wins than on the quality of the losses, which is why he places Texas ahead of Alabama.

The offense hasn't always looked like that of a national championship favorite. The résumé still belongs in the top six.

Indiana's 27-13 win over USC put another major obstacle behind the Hoosiers.

They are 9-1 and now control a straightforward path to the Big Ten Championship Game.

Chadwick still has Indiana below the one-loss teams with stronger signature wins, but the Hoosiers have continued doing enough to stay firmly in the top 10.

They visit Washington in Week 12 before closing with Purdue.

With an 88.4% playoff probability, Indiana's remaining job is simply to avoid a late collapse.

Tennessee moves ahead of Alabama in Chadwick's order for one obvious reason: The Volunteers beat Alabama.

Tennessee's overall résumé may not have the same depth, but Chadwick values the head-to-head result enough to break the tie in the Volunteers' favor.

The Week 11 performance helped. Tennessee went to Texas A&M and won 22-7.

The Volunteers now face LSU in what should be their most important remaining regular-season game.

Chadwick's biggest disagreement with the selection committee is Alabama.

The committee had the Crimson Tide at No. 3 before Week 11. Chadwick would have them ninth.

"I think Alabama is wildly overranked right now by the committee," Chadwick said.

That doesn't mean he thinks Alabama is bad.

The Crimson Tide have won three straight, including convincing results against LSU, Texas A&M, and Vanderbilt. Their losses to Georgia and Tennessee are also stronger than the losses carried by several teams around them.

Chadwick's issue is that teams such as Notre Dame, Miami, Texas, and Tennessee have arguments he finds more compelling.

Alabama is still a playoff team. He just doesn't view the Crimson Tide as a top-three team.

Texas Tech moves into Chadwick's top 10 after beating Oklahoma State 52-27.

The biggest difference is at quarterback.

Thomas Castellanos has added another dimension to Mack Leftwich's offense, and Texas Tech has scored at least 34 points in every game since he took over.

The Red Raiders are now 9-1 and have increased their playoff probability to 58.4%.

They also have a defense capable of holding up against stronger opponents, particularly with Trey White healthy again.

Chadwick initially considered Wake Forest for the No. 10 spot but gave Texas Tech the edge because he prefers the Red Raiders' résumé.

No team made a louder Week 11 statement than Wake Forest.

The Demon Deacons beat SMU 49-7 on the road and are now 9-1.

Since losing to Miami, Wake Forest has beaten Louisville, Stanford, NC State, Cal, Virginia, Merrimack, and SMU. Other than the three-point win over Louisville, each victory came by at least 24 points.

Chadwick believes Wake Forest is playing like one of the best teams in the country even if the résumé lacks the single marquee win Texas Tech owns.

That can change in the ACC Championship Game.

Wake Forest now has an 82.5% chance to make the playoff and a 98.4% chance to reach the conference title game.

The Cougars are 8-2 after beating Baylor 28-7 and remain in an awkward position because they're more likely to make the playoff than the Big 12 Championship Game.

Their strongest argument is the win over Notre Dame.

That result has become more valuable every week as the Irish continue climbing.

BYU needs to finish against Kansas and Cincinnati without another loss. If the Cougars reach 10-2, Chadwick believes they will have a serious at-large case even if they stay home during championship weekend.

The committee's Nov. 10 top five was Georgia, Utah, Alabama, UCLA, and Notre Dame.

Chadwick's order after Week 11 is Georgia, Utah, UCLA, Notre Dame, and Miami.

He still expects Alabama to make the playoff. PFN gives the Crimson Tide a 99.8% chance.

The dispute is over whether Alabama has earned one of the best seeds in the field.

Chadwick prefers UCLA's undefeated record, Notre Dame's win over Miami, Miami's body of work, Texas' collection of ranked victories, Indiana's one-loss record, and Tennessee's head-to-head win before getting to the Crimson Tide.

The committee will give its next answer Tuesday night.

#2667. Cavaliers' Evan Mobley out at least another week with toe injury suffered in win over Knicks

The Cleveland Cavaliers will be without Evan Mobley for at least another week.

Mobley suffered a right toe sprain last week during their matchup with the New York Knicks and has been sidelined ever since. That injury has since been confirmed, the team announced on Monday afternoon, and he will now undergo treatment over the next seven to 10 days.

Mobley went down in the final minutes of the Cavaliers' 115-107 win over the New York Knicks on Wednesday. He tried to get up to block at shot at Madison Square Garden, but ended up slamming to the court hard and awkwardly. He remained down for a moment, clearly shaken up, and he hasn't played since.

Coach Kenny Atkinson said Friday, ahead of the Cavs' loss to the Miami Heat, that it was just a "sprain" and that they didn't "expect it to be a long-term thing at all." Mobley missed that game and Saturday's win over the Dallas Mavericks as a result.

But instead of just a game or two, Mobley will need at least another full week to recover. If he's out just the seven days, he'd be able to return for their matchup with the Chicago Bulls next week at the United Center. That would mean he'd missed five total games.

Mobley has averaged 16.9 points and 7.3 rebounds per game this season, his sixth in the league. The 25-year-old is in the second year of a five-year, $269 million deal with the Cavaliers, who selected him with the No. 3 overall pick back in 2021 out of USC.

The Cavaliers will enter Monday night's matchup with the Bulls with a 7-7 record.

#2660. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2659. Jets QB Geno Smith avoids major injuries after leaving loss to Bills multiple times with concussion, ankle issue

Though he left Sunday's contest multiple times with various injuries, Geno Smith appears to have avoided anything major.

The New York Jets quarterback underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal any major issues, including on his ankle, according to the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Smith will continue to be evaluated this week, but he appears to be in a good spot to make the start again next Sunday for their contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Smith left Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills multiple times. He went down initially at the end of the first half when he was hit both high and low after throwing a pass, and he fell hard down to the ground on his back. He remained down for several moments before finally getting up and walking to the sideline medical tent.

Backup Cade Klubnik then took the field for the Jets to start the second half.

Smith returned after clearing concussion protocol, but then left the game the following possession after a big hit. He was then sidelined with an ankle injury the rest of the way.

Smith finished throwing 13-of-21 for 148 yards in the loss. Klubnik wasn't much better, and the Jets have now gone nine straight quarters without scoring a touchdown.

Smith has thrown for 2,226 yards with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions this season, his first back with the Jets since 2016. The team holds just a 2-8 record and is well out of the playoff hunt already. They are well within range of securing the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft at this point, too.

While the Jets haven't made a decision just yet, it sounds like Smith will be able to go in their matchup with the Chargers next weekend. The Chargers entered their Monday Night Football contest against the Baltimore Ravens as the league's only winless team, so Sunday will be a very big opportunity for Smith and the Jets to end their losing skid.

#2653. Cavs announce injury update for Evan Mobley

The Cleveland Cavaliers have announced that NBA All-Star Evan Mobley will be out for the next few games following a left great toe sprain suffered on November 11. Mobley sustained his injury against the New York Knicks.

Mobley will be re-evaluated after 7-10 days.

The Cavs' big man is averaging 16.9 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.5 blocks, and 1.1 steals per game. He's also shooting a career-high 47.9% from the three-point line. Mobley's increased floor spacing has been his biggest positive development at the start of the season.

Mobley isn't the only Cavalier who has been banged up. Sam Merrill is out with an elbow injury, Jaylon Tyson has been working through an ankle injury, and Nae'Qwan Tomlin has yet to make his season debut with a back injury.

These injuries have opened the door for younger players like Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor to rack up early minutes. This has paid off, with both Proctor and Thomas making the most of their increased opportunities. Norchad Omier is another player who deserves credit in this regard.

Still, the Cavs haven't been able to play with much consistency given the changes in their lineup on a nightly basis. This has led to a slower start than fans would like, with Cleveland posting a 7-7 record in their first 14 games.

Wins over the Dallas Mavericks with a depleted roster are encouraging. Losses to the Charlotte Hornets are not as much fun. Cleveland has much to figure out this regular season, and injuries won't make that any easier for them.

For now, the Cavs will be without Mobley for at least the next week, which includes games against the Memphis Grizzlies, Indiana Pacers, and another game against the Chicago Bulls next Monday.

Mobley's presence as an all-world defender and elite play finisher will be missed. But the Cavs will lean heavily on Jarrett Allen to hold down the fort in his absence, and an emphasis will be placed on Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant to step up and add further support.

#2652. The Packers’ offensive line regressed against the Vikings

We all saw the Green Bay Packers' offensive line get pushed around by the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but I'm sure some of you are wondering exactly why the team messed up in crucial situations over and over. Hopefully, you'll learn a little more about the game and the status of the team by the end of this article.

I want to start with this up front: I don't think the Packers' running game was actually that bad on Sunday — at least on the relative scale of Green Bay's running game. Where I really think the team regressed was in the pass protection department, where they played their worst game since at least the first three weeks of the season.

I clipped up all of the runs that the Packers' running backs had in the tweets above, if you want to check them out. There are a couple of poor calls (like the pin and pull sweep that had no chance because of Minnesota's defensive call), but for the most part, Green Bay got a hat on a hat against the Vikings, something we can't say of prior games.

Can they move anyone? No! They never have been able. They have one preferred starter on the field. Can they get in front of people, at least on the ground? The last two weeks are probably the Packers' best back-to-back performances this season.

The first big mistake the Packers made was on this duo run. The diagram above is what Green Bay's offensive line is expecting pre-snap. Because the Vikings stunted their three-technique defensive lineman outside on the play, though, right tackle Anthony Belton never gets off his block, and there's a free runner when the play should have gotten up to the safety level.

It's the second play in the Johnson cutup.

The second big mess-up was on this outside zone toss, where the team handled another stunt poorly. On paper, if everyone stays in the gaps they line up in, the diagram above is what the run should look like. Essentially, offensive linemen try to "scoop" defensive linemen to their play-side, and if there isn't a defender in that gap, they climb to the second level and try to work on backers and safeties, after first securing that no one stunted in their play-side gap pre-snap.

The problem is that the Vikings don't stay in their gaps, and they slant weak on the play. Because of this, there should be three pass-offs. The Packers don't execute a single one of them, leading to all three players getting penetration.

It's the play that you keep seeing screenshots of over and over again. It's the fourth play in the Johnson cutup.

These plays look like crap, but outside of that, the Packers mostly played their rules correctly this week — again, which has not been the case over most of the year. Over the last two weeks, they've found something that worked for them: running counter, a play that allows the offensive linemen to get on train tracks and just block downhill instead of worrying about assignments being exchanged by the Vikings' blitzes and stunts.

Everyone makes a wall of down blocks except for a kickout player (either a pulling guard or a tight end) and an insert player (again, either a pulling guard or tight end). As a reminder, the zone plays that didn't work against Minnesota are what Green Bay ran a lot of in the preseason and through Week 3 of the regular season. They went out of their way to try to get good at what they're doing the worst this year.

On counter and split zone concepts, the Packers had 10 carries for 50 yards (5 yards per carry) on the day. On other concepts, which mostly relied on changing targets post-snap, the Packers were just 6 for 6 (1 YPC).

My guess: Green Bay wanted to punish Minnesota with the ground game this week, particularly counter and split zone runs, but the game got out of hand and they had to ditch that script when they were down three scores. The team played a lot of extra tight end looks in this game, allowing the Vikings to get an extra player in the box on defense.

The passing game is really where the Packers' line struggled, in part because they were playing these multiple tight end sets that added just another variable for Green Bay's line to account for. Against Minnesota, the Packers looked completely lost on the interior offensive line, which was made up of Laken Tomlinson, John Williams and Travis Glover (left to right).

I thought we were over this. From Weeks 4-9, after the disaster that was the Atlanta Falcons game on Monday Night Football, the Packers had just a 35 pressure rate, good for the 16th-lowest in the NFL over this time. They looked like an average pass-protection unit over the last two months.

In the first three weeks of the year, the Packers cracked the 40 percent pressure rate twice, but had done it only once in the past six weeks. It seemed like they turned a corner, but then the Vikings came to town.

Yesterday, Minnesota posted a 60 percent pressure rate, the highest number that Green Bay has allowed all season. In Weeks 1-3 and 10, the Packers have allowed a 46 percent pressure rate overall, the highest mark in the league over those four weeks.

It's hard to know what Green Bay's offensive line will look like moving forward, because we just saw a huge regression after a streak of solid play.

Mind you, this all came with Love's time to throw at just 2.27 seconds against the Vikings, and they still sacked him eight times in this game. For perspective, the average NFL time to throw is around 2.8 seconds, so Love was operating about a half-second faster than the average. And he was still getting popped left and right. Had he held onto the ball at an average rate, the line's pressure rate would have been even higher.

Here are just a few clips of the Packers' offensive line blowing up plays from essentially the snap of the ball on Sunday, just to show how poor it was:

This tweet is supposed to say Belton, not Becton. I apologize to the Becton family.

All three interior offensive linemen had disaster games, looking consistently confused by Minnesota's defense. Right tackle also Anthony Belton struggled, as he's not a good athlete for the tackle position and should ideally be a guard at this level — but the injury to Zach Bako-Bewele forced him into his position this year.

Green Bay's plan to add extra bodies into the formation with multiple tight end sets kind of worked in the run game, where they were able to run counter and split zone runs pretty well against Minnesota, but they couldn't stick with the ground game once they went down multiple points — understandably. What really hurt on the ground was when the offensive line had to think and react to the Vikings' defensive front, and the line wasn't able to execute on those runs.

To make matters worse, the extra tight end (and offensive line) looks helped Minnesota bring an extra body in the box in the passing game, which adds exponentially more options for defensive coordinator Brian Flores for each body he could line up as a threat. Against those pressure fronts, the Packers' interior offensive line's heads were spinning all game.

Next time, maybe LaFleur will want to spread out the formation against those pressure looks, instead of having running backs and tight ends walk up to the line of scrimmage. It's what the Vikings did against Green Bay's pressure fronts, and Minnesota was able to get a good number of explosive plays in those situations, notably on third and long.

The Packers' offensive line just isn't good enough to deal with this many variables post-snap. They're not coached well enough. LaFleur, the head coach, just hasn't accepted that going into the second half of November. The offense looked better when they ditched their game plan in the second half of the third quarter, turning into a three-receiver spread team that ran the hurry-up no-huddle. The Packers went on a little run there and looked like they had a chance to get back into the game until they fumbled the ball on a kickoff return.

The fact that "do what you want, just play fast" led to better results than Green Bay's game plan is a damning indictment of the staff's decisions this week.

#2650. Rummenigge reveals remarkable conversation with Neuer that convinced goalkeeper to join Bayern

Since joining Bayern Munich from Schalke 04 in 2011, Manuel Neuer has established himself as a club legend and one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time.

As Bayern's chairman at the time, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was heavily involved in the negotiations that ultimately led to the shot-stopper making the switch to Munich.

In an interview with Bundesliga.com, the 71-year-old looked back on a particular episode following a game between Bayern and Schalke ahead of Neuer's move – an encounter that proved decisive in convincing the goalkeeper to join the Bavarian giants.

“We had a DFB Cup semi-final against Schalke, and our coach at the time, Louis van Gaal, made a comment that wasn’t particularly flattering. He said we didn’t really need Manuel Neuer. We had Thomas Kraft in goal, who was OK, but Manuel Neuer was already on a completely different level,” Rummenigge recalled, adding:

"Our ultras in the Südkurve put up their banners and there were verbal insults and so on. I remember Uli and I sitting together, absolutely furious. We lost the first leg, and Manuel Neuer had played like a god. Unfortunately, he was still on the wrong side at Schalke at the time.

"After the game, I went down to the dressing room area. I bumped into Horst Heldt, who was Schalke’s sporting director at the time. I asked him, ‘Horst, could I have a quick word with Manuel?’ We were already quite far along in our discussions with Schalke about bringing him to Bayern. He said yes.

"Manuel came out wearing nothing but a towel, and I told him, ‘Manuel, I want to apologise unreservedly for what happened. It was disgraceful, and we won’t simply carry on as if nothing had happened.’

"He replied as though nothing had happened and asked me just one question: ‘Are you and Mr Hoeneß in favour of me coming?’ I said, ‘Of course. We’ll do everything we can to bring you here. You’re the most important signing we could make.’ He said, ‘Then I’ll come.’

“I remember thinking that, after everything he’d been through, he still stood by us. I’ll never forget that.”

Rummenigge also spoke at length about how Neuer has transformed the art of goalkeeping and the influence he has had on Bayern.

“He changed everything. No one else had done what he did. Goalkeeping used to have very little to do with playing with your feet, or with football itself. In his first year with Pep Guardiola, he completely revolutionised the position,” he said.

"I remember him sometimes standing 40 or 50 metres outside his own goal. Then those long balls would come and he’d deal with them, sometimes with what I always call his ‘heel, toe, tip’ technique.

“The spectators would give him a standing ovation as he played the ball to a team-mate in the outfield with pinpoint precision. He revolutionised goalkeeping, and that’s how the position is interpreted today. I have to say that the origins of the modern goalkeeping game lie with Manuel,” added Rummenigge, declaring Neuer the best goalkeeper Bayern have ever had, ahead of other club legends such as Sepp Maier and Oliver Kahn.
